entities.summary:
Khui was an ancient Egyptian king and/or nomarch during the early First Intermediate Period, whose existence has been debated among historians due to the scarcity of archaeological records.

Khui may have belonged to the Eighth Dynasty of Egypt, as Jürgen Beckerath has proposed, or he may instead have been a provincial nomarch who proclaimed himself king. His potential reign would have occurred sometime between the 22nd and 21st centuries BCE, during a period of significant instability and fragmentation in ancient Egypt.

The lack of concrete evidence regarding Khui's reign makes it difficult to assess the full extent of his impact on Egyptian history. However, it is clear that his legacy would have been felt by the subsequent dynasties, which would have had to navigate the complexities of the First Intermediate Period.

Khui's legacy is also tied to the broader cultural and historical context of ancient Egypt during this period, which saw the rise of new religious and artistic traditions, as well as the emergence of new regional powers.

One of the most striking aspects of Khui's legacy is the enduring debate among historians about his very existence. Despite the paucity of evidence, Khui remains a fascinating figure, whose story speaks to the complexities and challenges of ancient Egyptian history.
